content.title: Bodo/Glimt vs Spurs: Champions League tips and odds
content.text: Our expert has two tips for the Champions League match between Bodo/Glimt and Tottenham Hotspur at the Aspmyra Stadion on Tuesday (kick-off, 8pm BST). Match details What: Bodo/Glimt vs Tottenham, Champions League Where: Aspmyra Stadion, Norway When: 8pm, Tuesday September 30 Where to watch: TNT Sports 2 & TNT Sports 6 Norwegian club can call the shots Four months after they defeated Bodo/Glimt 5-1 on aggregate en route to Europa League glory, Tottenham Hotspur return to the Arctic Circle to reconvene with the Norwegian side tonight but this time the teams square up in the Champions League. Since their last meeting with Spurs, Bodo/Glimt have been racking up the wins in the Norwegian Eliteserien, while they defeated Sturm Graz of Austria 6-2 on aggregate in the Champions League play-offs. Their opening game of this season’s Champions League was a frenetic 2-2 draw away to Slavia Prague with the Norwegians recovering from 2–0 down after 74 minutes to salvage a point. They were lively in that game, which produced 37 shots, including 21 on target, and 10 of those efforts on target came from Bodo/Glimt. Spurs, meanwhile, have changed manager since that meeting and Thomas Frank’s first Champions League game as head coach was a bit of a snoozefest with his side edging Villarreal 1-0 thanks to an own goal from Luiz Junior. There was just one shot on target in that game and Tottenham lost the shot count 10-9 against the Spaniards, despite home advantage. On Saturday, meanwhile, Tottenham only just outshot lowly Wolves 10-9 in a 1-1 draw in the Premier League, despite the fact they were chasing the game after going 1-0 down in the 54th minute. They rank 11th in the Premier League this term for total xG (expected goals) with just 6.95 from six games and are in the same position for average shots per game with 11.3 per match. Under Ange Postecoglou, Spurs defended well in the Europa League semi-final between the sides in Norway in May and, given it can be such a tough place to visit, they may take a cautious approach to the game again. They are still missing key forward Dominic Solanke and Bodo/Glimt look a value bet to register more shots on target than Spurs at 6/4. Back Berg to test Spurs keeper If Bodo/Glimt do rack up the shots as we expect in this game, one player worth looking at to have a shot on target is midfielder Patrick Berg, who is overpriced at 10/11. Berg may play at the heart of the Bodo/Glimt midfield but he is not afraid to get forward, as shown by the fact he managed 27 shots, including 11 on target, in last season’s Europa League.
